messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@legacybank.com>, Sandra Li <sandra.li@legacybank.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: On-prem air-gap qualification & next steps

Hi Tom & Sandra,

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through your use case and constraints. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap:
- Deployment preference: LegacyBank is targeting a private, on-prem, air-gapped deployment for PII/QC workloads; you noted occasional bursts that may require offline upgrades/maintenance windows.
- Security constraints: strict egress restrictions, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and SOC2 + internal audit checklist.
- Ops constraints: upgrades must be performed offline; limited external access for package pulls; patching windows twice per quarter.
- Hardware: you have a mix of 2U racks and a handful of GPU-capable nodes today; exact GPU counts TBD.

Open items / asks for next step workshop:
1) Hardware requirements: please confirm expected GPU model (A100/H100), per-node CPU/w RAM, and whether you can reserve dedicated NICs (10/25/100Gb). I attached an initial requirements workbook to make that easy.
2) Offline upgrade approach: we proposed three models (airgap installer, removable media, and on-site image apply). Please confirm which approach aligns with your change control.
3) Maintenance windows & runbook ownership: who on your ops team will own on-site procedures and who requires runbook-level approvals?

Attachments: redwood_onprem_playbook.pdf (our standard air-gapped playbook), initial_hw_requirements.xlsx (fill in hardware counts).

Next steps:
- You: fill hardware workbook and return by EOD Friday (3 Dec).
- Us: draft an offline upgrade options doc and a proposed runbook template (I’ll send by tomorrow).
- Schedule: follow-up workshop next week to deep-dive HW + upgrade process — suggest Tue 12/1 9:00am PT.

If it helps, I can loop in our infra lead (Dev Patel) to review the hardware checklist in the workshop.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Marissa, thanks for the clear summary. A few quick answers and some follow-ups from our security team: 

Hardware answers (high-level):
- GPU: primary preference is NVIDIA H100 for new nodes; we do have some older A100 nodes but want H100 for production.
- CPU/memory: typical servers are 2x 32-core CPUs, 512GB RAM.
- Network: 25Gb is preferred; we can do 10Gb for a subset.
- Storage: local NVMe for model weights, central NFS for data/outputs.

Security/ops questions:
- OS & image management: can Redwood support a pre-baked OS image (our team will provide) or must the image be created by Redwood? We cannot allow image downloads from the public internet.
- Upgrade mechanism: we need an offline image apply flow and an offline package bundle (removable media). Does Redwood support an air-gap installer that runs solely from local media?
- Audit: our auditors want details on upgrade signing and rollback procedures.

I’ve attached our internal requirements doc for your reference. 

We can target the 12/1 workshop but need it to be under 60 minutes. 9:00am PT works for Sandra and me.

Tom

Hi Tom & Sandra — thanks for the quick response and the requirements doc. Answers inline below and next steps for the workshop: 

- Pre-baked OS image: Yes — Redwood can operate with a customer-provided, pre-baked OS image. Our installer supports an image import process that runs entirely from local media; we will not require internet access to deploy the runtime. We’ll need a checksum/signing key and the exact image details in advance.

- Air-gap installer / removable media: We support two patterns: (A) removable-media installer that executes the full stack install locally, and (B) image-based deployment where the OS+runtime are delivered as a pre-built image. Both paths support offline package bundles for patches. I attached a short note on upgrade options.

- Upgrade signing & rollback: Redwood signs our upgrade bundles with a customer-visible checksum and supports staged rollback. For the workshop we’ll bring our signing/verification flow and an example runbook.

Workshop: Tue 12/1, 9:00am PT — invite sent. Agenda: 1) HW confirmation, 2) Upgrade & air-gap installer pattern, 3) Runbook & audit evidence, 4) Next steps and timeline.

Action: Dev — can you confirm the difference in perf/throughput and recommended network/storage config for H100 vs A100 for our inference profiles (low-latency, bursty batch)? Also prepare a short slide on offline upgrade steps.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: HW & offline ops notes for LegacyBank workshop

Marissa / Michael — quick internal notes to prep for the 9:00 workshop: 

1) H100 vs A100 perf: H100 gives ~1.6x throughput for fp16 inferencing across our kernels; for quantized int8 the gap narrows but H100 still performs better on large batch sizes. If they plan to run mixed workloads (low-latency + nightly batch), recommend H100 for production and A100 for dev/test.

2) Network: target 25Gb for compute nodes; management plane can be 10Gb. For model sync we prefer 25Gb+ or NVMe-to-NVMe copy to speed weight distribution during upgrades.

3) Power & racks: call out dual PDUs per rack and per-node power draw (H100 ~ 700W per card). Need them to confirm rack PDU capacity.

4) Offline upgrade tooling: we’ll standardize on an airgap installer that consumes a signed tarball and a signed image. For larger clusters we support a staged apply (canary nodes then full rollout). Bring runbook templates and a checksum verification example.

5) Action items for workshop:
- I’ll prepare two slides (perf comparison + recommended network/storage).
- Bring a sample runbook showing canary rollback steps.
- Confirm we have the legacybank requirement doc loaded to the shared Drive link.

Will sync with you 15 minutes before the call.

—Dev
